html:
The Sonderbund War of November 1847 was a short civil war in which the Liberal Protestant cantons defeated a separate league, the Sonderbund, of seven Catholic, conservative cantons.

The Catholic cantons, led by Lucerne, had formed their league in 1845 after radicals pushed to close monasteries and to make the loose confederation into a stronger state. The federal diet ruled the league illegal. General Guillaume-Henri Dufour led the federal army and won in under a month, with fewer than a hundred dead on both sides.

Dufour's restraint helped the losers accept the result. The next year the federal constitution created modern Switzerland. Dufour went on to help found the Red Cross. Abroad, the war was a prelude to the revolutions of 1848.
sum: The Sonderbund War of November 1847 was a short civil war in which the Liberal Protestant cantons defeated a separate league, the Sonderbund, of seven Catholic, conservative cantons.
